title: Consensus-Breaking Global Hopf Bifurcation in Memory-Based Multi-Agent Systems
summary: This dissertation provides the first systematic study of symmetric consensus-breaking bifurcation to periodic multiconsensus in multi-agent systems. It analyzes this for three classes of multi-agent systems based on three different types of memory, whose closed-loop dynamics equations form delay differential equations of retarded type, neutral type, and pseudoneutral type - a subclassification of retarded type equations introduced in this dissertation which bridges retarded and neutral type delay equations. Equivariant twisted degree is used to analyze the symmetric global Hopf bifurcation…
